speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned a rear-end collision resulting in right groin pain and abnormal leg positioning; can you describe exactly how your leg is positioned and if you heard a snap or crack at the time of the accident?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Femoral Neck Fracture.

The mechanism of injury (rear-end collision with restrained driver status), immediate onset of severe right groin pain, and abnormal leg positioning are classic presentations for a femoral neck fracture. This is a medical emergency requiring immediate orthopedic intervention to prevent avascular necrosis. Please proceed to emergency radiography of the right hip.
